rules.title: No authorization attributes anywhere in a web application
rules.precondition: The project references Microsoft.AspNetCore.* or is a web/Blazor/API project.
rules.why: Zero authorization attributes in a web application means every endpoint, page and mutation is reachable anonymously.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Check for a global fallback policy (SetFallbackPolicy / AddAuthorization with a default policy / an authorization middleware convention) before reporting - that is a valid alternative to per-endpoint attributes.

rules.title: Authentication services not registered in the host
rules.why: Without the authentication and authorization middleware registered, [Authorize] attributes elsewhere are inert and the whole app is anonymous.
rules.falsePositiveHints: An API fronted by a gateway that enforces authN can be legitimate - but only if that gateway is verifiable. Ask rather than assume; if unverifiable, report as High with the assumption stated.

rules.title: AllowAnonymous on a data-modifying or sensitive endpoint
rules.why: AllowAnonymous punches a hole through an otherwise-protected surface; on a write endpoint it is an unauthenticated mutation.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Login, health, error and static public pages are legitimate. Read what the action does before flagging.

rules.title: Blazor SignalR hub mapped without an authorization requirement
rules.why: An open hub lets an anonymous client establish a circuit and invoke server-side component logic, bypassing page-level checks.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Closed if the call chains .RequireAuthorization() or a global fallback policy covers it.

rules.title: Raw SQL execution API in use
rules.why: Raw SQL is only safe with parameters. Interpolated or concatenated raw SQL is directly injectable.
rules.falsePositiveHints: FromSqlInterpolated and FromSql (EF Core 7+) parameterize automatically - NOT findings. FromSqlRaw with only DbParameter arguments is safe. The finding is concatenation or $"..." interpolation of non-constant values into the SQL text.

rules.title: HTML rendered without encoding
rules.why: These bypass Razor/Blazor automatic encoding. Any untrusted content reaching them executes as script in the victim's session.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Not a finding over a compile-time literal or content produced by a trusted, escaping Markdown/sanitizer library. Trace the value's origin.

rules.title: Content Security Policy weakened with unsafe directives
rules.why: unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval remove most of CSP's value as an XSS mitigation.
rules.falsePositiveHints: style-src 'unsafe-inline' is often unavoidable with component libraries (MudBlazor, Blazorise) and is materially lower risk than script-src. Distinguish the two directives; do not report them at the same severity.

rules.title: No security headers middleware detected
rules.why: Without these headers the browser applies no clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, transport or content-injection defenses.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Headers may be set by a reverse proxy or CDN. If so, note it and downgrade to Info - but ask for evidence rather than assuming.

rules.title: HTTPS redirection or HSTS absent
rules.why: Without redirection and HSTS, a first request over HTTP exposes session cookies and credentials to interception.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Frequently terminated at a load balancer. Verify rather than assume, and record which.

rules.title: Antiforgery / CSRF protection not configured
rules.precondition: Web app with cookie-based authentication and state-changing form posts. Not applicable to a pure token-authenticated API.
rules.why: Cookie-authenticated state changes without an antiforgery token can be triggered cross-site from any page the victim visits.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Not applicable to stateless bearer-token APIs. Establish the auth model before reporting.

rules.title: Detailed errors or developer exception page potentially enabled outside development
rules.why: Framework-detail error pages disclose stack traces, file paths and configuration to anyone who can trigger an error.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Correct when gated by env.IsDevelopment(). Read the surrounding condition; report only when it is ungated or the production config sets it.

rules.title: Permissive CORS policy
rules.why: A wildcard origin combined with credentials lets any site read authenticated responses on the user's behalf.
rules.falsePositiveHints: AllowAnyOrigin without AllowCredentials on a genuinely public read-only API is Low. AllowAnyOrigin + AllowCredentials is rejected by the framework, so look for SetIsOriginAllowed(_ => true) + AllowCredentials - that combination is the real High.

rules.title: No server-side validation annotations on models or DTOs
rules.precondition: Application accepts user input through forms or API bodies.
rules.why: Client-side validation is a usability feature, not a control. Without server-side validation, malformed and over-length input reaches the data layer.
rules.falsePositiveHints: FluentValidation, minimal-API filters or manual guard clauses are valid alternatives - search for those before reporting.

rules.title: Entity bound directly to a request (mass assignment risk)
rules.why: Binding a persistence entity straight from the request body lets a caller set fields the UI never exposes - roles, prices, owner ids, audit columns.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Binding to a purpose-built DTO with only the intended fields is correct. Check what the bound type actually contains.

rules.title: Cookie or session security attributes weakened
rules.why: A session cookie without HttpOnly is readable by injected script; without Secure it is sent over cleartext.
rules.falsePositiveHints: SameSite=None is legitimate for genuine cross-site flows, but only paired with Secure. Verify the pairing.

rules.title: Weak password or lockout policy
rules.why: Relaxed password rules and disabled lockout make credential stuffing and brute force practical.
rules.falsePositiveHints: NIST SP 800-63B favors length and breach-list checks over composition rules; a long minimum with relaxed composition is acceptable modern practice. Judge the policy as a whole.

rules.title: No audit logging on write paths
rules.precondition: Application performs create/update/delete operations on business data.
rules.why: Without an audit trail on mutations, neither incident response nor dispute resolution can establish who changed what.
rules.falsePositiveHints: EF Core interceptors, SaveChanges overrides or a database-level audit trigger also satisfy this. Look for them before reporting.

rules.title: Package references to inventory for advisory checking
rules.why: Collects the dependency inventory that the Step 4 advisory check operates on.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Not a finding on its own. Feed the results into the dependency check and report only confirmed advisories, plus the absence of automated scanning.
